title: Missing authorization on deployment.killProcess/readLogs/removeDeployment and host-level schedule reads (cross-organization)
summary:
## Summary

For deployments that belong to a host-level schedule (`scheduleType: "dokploy-server"`, i.e. no `applicationId`/`composeId` and no `schedule.serverId`), `deployment.killProcess` performs no authorization check. Any authenticated user of any organization who knows the `deploymentId` can make the Dokploy server run `kill -9 <stored pid>` on the Dokploy host. The same gap in `schedule.one` and `deployment.allByType` lets that user read the host schedule (including its script) and its deployments, which discloses the `deploymentId`.

## Affected version

- Verified on: Dokploy v0.30.10 (self-hosted)
- Code unchanged on `canary` at d64ebedd0

## Code (canary)

- `apps/dokploy/server/api/routers/deployment.ts:212-242`: `killProcess` checks access only when `applicationId || composeId` or `schedule.serverId` is set; otherwise falls through. It also does not check `deployment.status`, so the stored pid is killed even after the deployment finished.
- `apps/dokploy/server/api/routers/deployment.ts:132-153`: `allByType` with `type: "schedule"` has the same fall-through.
- `apps/dokploy/server/api/routers/schedule.ts:288-313`: `schedule.one` only checks `schedule: ["read"]` (granted to members) and an org check for `scheduleType === "server"`; `dokploy-server` schedules are not org-checked, although `schedule.list` restricts them to owner/admin (`schedule.ts:238-249`).
- pid source: `packages/server/src/services/schedule.ts:202` and `packages/server/src/utils/schedules/utils.ts:154-166`.

## Preconditions

- Victim org has a host-level ("Dokploy server") schedule. Creating these is owner/admin only.
- Attacker is a plain `member` of a different organization on the same instance (or the same org; members cannot list host schedules).
- Attacker knows the `scheduleId` or `deploymentId` (nanoid). I did not find an enumeration path; the reads below disclose the `deploymentId` once the `scheduleId` is known.

## Reproduction (local test instance only)

1. As owner of org A: create a host schedule with script `sleep 600` and run it (`schedule.create` with `scheduleType: "dokploy-server"`, then `schedule.runManually`). Inside the Dokploy container: `26321 bash -c ./script.sh`, `26322 sleep 600`.
2. As a plain member of org B (not a member of org A):

```
curl -s -b memberB.jar -H "origin: http://127.0.0.1:13000" \
  "http://127.0.0.1:13000/api/schedule.one?scheduleId=<scheduleId>"
# -> full schedule of org A, incl. "script":"sleep 600", "organizationId":"<orgA>"

curl -s -b memberB.jar -H "origin: http://127.0.0.1:13000" \
  "http://127.0.0.1:13000/api/deployment.allByType?id=<scheduleId>&type=schedule"
# -> [{"deploymentId":"<id>","status":"running","logPath":"/etc/dokploy/schedules/...", ...}]

curl -s -b memberB.jar -H "origin: http://127.0.0.1:13000" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"deploymentId":"<id>"}' http://127.0.0.1:13000/api/deployment.killProcess
# -> 200, empty body
```

## Observed result

- After the call, pid 26321 (`bash -c ./script.sh`) was gone and the deployment status changed to `error`. (The `sleep` child survived because only the parent pid is killed.)
- Calling `killProcess` again on the finished deployment executed `kill -9 26321` again: `Command failed: kill -9 26321 ... No such process`. There is no status check, so a stale pid is killed whenever this is called.
- Control: member B calling `schedule.list` with `scheduleType: "dokploy-server"` gets `403 Only owners and admins can list host-level schedules`.

## Additional affected procedures (found while fixing)

`deployment.readLogs` and `deployment.removeDeployment` have the same fall-through as `killProcess`: they check access only when the deployment has `applicationId`/`composeId` or `schedule.serverId`, and otherwise do nothing. Deployments that only carry a parent id fall through: host schedules, but also deployments of application/compose schedules (they store only `scheduleId`), backups, volume backups, preview deployments and server...
